messages:
acme_infra: Hey team — our service started failing to call Redwood private inference endpoint from our VPC this morning. SDK errors: `tls: handshake failure` and sometimes `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. No config change on our side.

alex_w: sorry to hear that — can you paste the root error + a minimal repro curl -v to the endpoint? also confirm if this is from ECS tasks in private subnet or from EC2?

acme_infra: repro from an EC2 bastion in the same private subnet (no internet egress except via NAT). curl we ran: `curl -v https://inference.acme-prod-redwood.internal:443 -o /dev/null` returns `* Failed to connect to inference.acme-prod-redwood.internal port 443: Connection timed out` then `TLS handshake timeout`. We also see intermittent `handshake failure` in app logs.

maria_s: okay, two possible layers: DNS/resolution -> route/NAT -> SG/NACL blocking -> TLS interception/MTLS issue. can you run `dig +short inference.acme-prod-redwood.internal` and `traceroute -T -p 443 inference.acme-prod-redwood.internal` from the bastion?

acme_infra: dig returns the internal ip (10.20.5.12). traceroute TCP shows first few hops then `* * *` after NAT gateway IP. pasted: `traceroute to 10.20.5.12 (10.20.5.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets 1 10.0.1.1 0.6 ms 0.5 ms 0.5 ms 2 10.0.254.1 1.1 ms 1.0 ms 0.9 ms 3 10.0.254.254 3.2 ms * *`

alex_w: that suggests packets are hitting NAT/gw and not returning. can you run a tcpdump on the bastion while attempting curl? `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 tcp and host 10.20.5.12 and port 443`

acme_infra: tcpdump shows `IP 10.0.1.12.56732 > 10.20.5.12.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]` then no SYN-ACK back. after a few retransmits we get RST from 10.0.254.254 (NAT).

srinivasan_r: interesting. If NAT is sending RST, it likely did not see an established conn mapping, maybe because NACL on the downstream subnet is blocking ephemeral port return traffic, or there is a symmetric routing path. For stateless NACLs you need explicit allow rules for both directions including ephemeral ranges. What are your subnet NACL rules for the private subnets and the Redwood endpoint subnet?

acme_infra: NACL shown: rule 100 allow TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0, rule 110 deny all 0.0.0.0/0 (high-level). There are no explicit ephemeral port allows. Security groups: bastion has SG-egress 0.0.0.0/0:443 allowed. Redwood SG allows inbound 443 from our CIDR.

maria_s: that deny-all at the bottom is fine only if earlier rules cover all necessary ephemeral ranges. For TCP client connections, return traffic uses ephemeral ports on the client side (1024-65535 or AWS uses 32768-65535 for some AMIs). Because NACLs are stateless, you must allow ephemeral range inbound/outbound depending on direction. Right now you allow 443 but not the ephemeral return — NAT sees SYN out but reply gets dropped by NACL, NAT drops mapping and RSTs the session.

acme_infra: ahhh that explains it. we found docs that AWS recommended ephemeral range 1024-65535. our infra team uses a tight NACL policy.

alex_w: two remediation paths: 1) add explicit allow rules in the NACL for ephemeral range both directions (ingress and egress) so return packets are permitted; 2) move the workload behind a managed NAT/Transit gateway with permissive return path and use SGs for control. Also consider limiting ephemeral range to the commonly used subset (e.g., 32768-60999) to keep rule count small.

acme_infra: doing a quick test — added NACL rule 120 allow TCP ephemeral 32768-60999 from 0.0.0.0/0 (both ingress/egress).

ops_bot: deploy-bot: NACL rule 120 applied to subnet-priv-1 by infra-ci at 2024-11-06T09:44:12Z :white_check_mark:

acme_infra: retesting curl now... `curl -v https://inference.acme-prod-redwood.internal:443 -o /dev/null` now shows `* Connected to inference.acme-prod-redwood.internal (10.20.5.12) port 443 (#0)` then `* TLS handshake completed` then `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` :)

maria_s: great. are you still seeing any `x509` errors? those usually mean an MTLS mismatch or private CA not trusted.

acme_infra: the `x509` errors stopped as well. we had some older containers that cached a cert bundle but after restart they picked up system CA.

srinivasan_r: notes for the ticket: root cause — overly restrictive stateless NACL blocking ephemeral client port ranges caused NAT to drop established mapping, resulting in TLS handshake timeouts and connection resets. fix — added ephemeral TCP allow range (32768-60999) and confirmed connectivity. recommendations — prefer security groups for coarse control, keep NACLs permissive for ephemeral ranges, add monitoring/packet capture on NAT for quicker triage, and document required NACL rules in runbook.

alex_w: I'll attach the repro commands and tcpdump snippet to the ticket, plus suggested remediation text for ops playbook.

acme_infra: thanks everyone — connectivity restored and we'll roll the NACL change to other regions. really appreciate the fast help :raised_hands:

maria_s: closing loop — follow up with infra to standardize ephemeral-range rule and add an egress allowlist test in CI.

ops_bot: incident-tracker: ticket #INC-2024-1421 updated: resolved -> monitoring for 24h.
